Vs.

full_judgment:
Sheikh Abdul Awal J: By this Rule the opposite Party No. 1 was called upon to show cause as to why the impugned order dated 16-7-2008 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka in Title Execution Case No. 14 of 2006 rejecting the application filed by the petitioners under Order XXI rule 26 of the Code of Civil Procedure for staying all further proceedings of Title Execution Case No. 14 of 2006 should not be set-aside. 

 3. The opposite party No. 1 as plaintiff after obtaining ex parte decree dated 12-1-2004 passed in Title Suit No. 85 of 1999 put the decree into execution by filing Title Execution Case No. 14 of 2006 before the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka. 

 4. During the pendency of the said execution case the present petitioners 3rd party filed an application under Order XXI rule 26 of the Code of Civil Procedure for staying all further proceeding of the Code of Civil Procedure for staying all further proceeding of the execution Case till disposal of the Title Suit No. 370 of 2007. 

 7. Mr Kabirul Islam Fakir, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners submits that the executing Court without considering the facts and circumstances of the case under misconception of law most illegally rejected the application filed by the present petitioners under Order XXI rule 26 CPC. He next in the course of argument after placing the provisional application and other materials on record including the impugned order dated 16-7-2008 submits that the present petitioners as plaintiffs filed Title Suit No. 370 of 2007 for setting-aside the ex parte judgment and decree of Title Suit No. 85 of 1999 and during pendency of the said Title Suit if the execution Case is completed by executing and registering the sale deed and handing over formal possession through Court the Title Suit No. 370 of 2007 would be frustrated and its result would be ineffective but the executing Court without considering the aspect of the case mechanically rejected the application for staying all further proceedings of Title Execution Case No. 14 of 2006 which resulted in the failure of justice and, as such, the impugned order is liable to be set-aside. 

 8. Mr Kabirul Islam Fakir, the learned Advocate finally submits that the executing Court ought to have considered that the petitioners are the owner and possessors of the suit properties and they filed Title Suit No. 370 of 2007 challenging the ex parte judgment and decree of Title Suit No. 85 of 1999, if the execution case arising out of ex parte judgment and decree of Title Suit No. 85 of 1999 is not stayed till disposal of the Title Suit No. 370 of 2007 the whole purpose of the Title Suit No. 370 of 2007 would be frustrated. 

 10. We have heard the learned Advocates, perused the Provisional application, counter affidavit and other connected papers as filed therewith. As already noticed that during the pendency of the execution case the present petitioners as 3rd party filed an application for staying all further proceedings of Title Execution Case No. 14 of 2006 arising out of Title Suit No. 85 of 1999 stating, inter alia, that on knowing about the said ex parte dectiee the petitioners as plaintiffs filed Title Suit No. 370 of 2007 before the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka for setting aside the said ex parte decree and in such situation if the proceedings of the execution case is not stayed the whole purpose of Title Suit No. 370 of 2007 would be frustrated. 

 12. Now, the real question for consideration in this Case is, whether the executing Court acted wrongly in holding that the petitioners being a third party to the decree has no locus standi to maintain an application for stay of the execution proceeding as per provisions of order XXI rule 26 and 29 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 17. In the instant case the petitioners being a third party of the ex parte decree filed an application under Order XXI rule 26 and 29 of the Code of Civil Procedure for staying all further proceedings of execution Case till disposal of the Title Suit No. 370 of 2007 and therefore, we are of the opinion that the executing Court in the facts and circumstances of the case rightly arrived at a finding that petitioners being a third party to the decree have no locus standi to file an application under Order XXI rule 26 and 29 of the Code of Civil Procedure for staying all further proceedings of Execution Case till disposal of the title Suit No. 370 of 2007. We endorse the reasoning given by the executing Court in rejecting the application under Order XXI rule 26 and 29 of the Code of Civil Procedure for stay. 

 19. In the result, the Rule is discharged without any order as to cost. The order of stay granted earlier by this Court stands vacated the executing Court is directed to proceed with the execution case expeditiously.
